caveat: Model estimate from a synthetic Halvian calibrated to the case brief. It shows which levers matter and how large the payoff could be under stated assumptions. It is not evidence from a real hospital.

break_even.explanation: The tool pays for itself when it saves about 6 minutes per admission: $500,000 a year / ($350 per bed-hour x 13,600 admissions a year) = 0.105 hours, about 6 minutes.

scenarios.name: Cautious
scenarios.settings: Today's default settings: staff act on 50% of flags within about 1 hour, alert threshold 70% (moving with crowding), discharges on the rounds list 1 hour earlier, and no credit for the bed board.

scenarios.name: Expected
scenarios.settings: Today's defaults plus the Live Bed Board, which we assume cuts the housekeeping notification delay and bed request processing by 25%.

scenarios.name: Full rollout
scenarios.settings: Staff act on 75% of flags, alert threshold 60% (moving with crowding), discharges on the rounds list 2 hours earlier, and the bed board on.

staffing_alternative.assumption: One clerical bed coordinator on every shift, 24 hours a day all year (8,760 hours), at the brief's $35 an hour administrative rate.
One more case manager on the 8-hour day shift every day of the year (2,920 hours), at the brief's $65 an hour nurse rate.
Two extra ED nurses on overtime for the day and evening shifts (16 hours each) on the busiest 10% of days (37 a year), at the brief's $65 an hour times 1.5.

tool_cost.note: Our ballpark of $550K to $650K over 18 months (the itemized budget comes to about $610K), spread evenly over 1.5 years; after Month 18 the running cost falls to about $210K a year.

references.source: Johns Hopkins study of discharge predictions in multidisciplinary rounds
references.finding: Feeding machine learning discharge predictions into daily rounds was followed by stays more than 12 hours shorter on 2 of 4 units (a medicine and a telemetry unit), with no change on the other two.

references.source: Proactive Inpatient Bed Requests for ED Admissions (2026 preprint, simulation)
references.finding: In a simulation, hourly bed requests driven by admission predictions cut ED boarding by 30 to 70%; it is a preprint, not a live deployment.

least_certain: The least certain assumption is the bed board's 25% cut in bed turnover delays: no study we found backs it, it alone adds 10 to 15 minutes per admission, and so the Cautious range leaves it out.
